name: Mezzotint Ground
desc: A copper plate rocked all over until it prints solid velvet black, then burnished back into light — heavy volumes surface out of the dark with no outline at all, only a raking lamp crawling across them, the burr grain never quite scraped away.

energy.doc: how hard the raking lamp bites — relief exaggeration, specular burnish, x-ray density

density.doc: how many volumes are worked into the plate (3 to 10)

speed.doc: rate multiplier on the drifting volumes and the lamp

scale.doc: size of the volumes against the plate

hue.doc: ink hue — 32 is a warm printer's black, drives paper and toning too

x.doc: centre of the worked area, x

y.doc: centre of the worked area, y

grain.doc: how much rocker burr survives the burnishing

act.doc: multi-minute program: steady plate / the lights are worked open and re-rocked / the tonal range compresses through aquatint bite stages

style.doc: aesthetic: velvet warm-black burr / hard-stepped tonal bite with rosin speckle / smooth outline-free light modelling, no grain / warm sepia old-master proof / clinical negative built from accumulated density instead of surface light

seed.doc: deterministic plate — rocker ground, volume placement and sizes
